articles.title: Former Canadian premier Danny Williams donated 185 acres of family land to protect rare lichens; the gift expands a Newfoundland nature reserve to 1,198 acres
articles.summary: Former Newfoundland and Labrador premier Danny Williams and his family have donated 75 hectares, or about 185 acres, of family land to the Nature
articles.body: Former Newfoundland and Labrador premier Danny Williams and his family have donated 75 hectares, or about 185 acres, of family land to the Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) to protect rare lichen habitat. The land, located north of St. Catharines in Newfoundland and Labrador, has been added to the Salmonier River Nature Reserve, bringing the protected area to 485 hectares, or roughly 1,198 acres. The donation followed an NCC survey that found boreal felt lichen on the Williams family property. The species is listed as being of special concern under Canada’s Species at Risk Act and grows in only a few areas around the world. The newly protected land also contains forests and wetlands supporting other species at risk.How Danny Williams' family land became important habitat for rare lichens in NewfoundlandThe conservation project began after the Nature Conservancy of Canada approached Williams in September 2023 about the possibility of rare lichens growing on his family’s land. NCC subsequently organised a targeted lichen survey, which confirmed the presence of boreal felt lichen, a tree-dwelling species that is listed as special concern in Newfoundland under Schedule 1 of the federal Species at Risk Act. The survey also found blue felt lichen and frosted glass-whiskers lichen nearby, both of which are also listed as special concern. The findings prompted discussions about permanently protecting the property and its unusual habitat.Why Danny Williams donated 185 acres to expand the Salmonier River Nature ReserveWilliams and his family donated 75 hectares of their land to NCC, allowing it to become part of the existing Salmonier River Nature Reserve. The addition increased the reserve from its previous size to 485 hectares, or approximately 1,198 acres. NCC said the expanded reserve and its habitats will be conserved for generations. Williams described himself as a long-time advocate for environmental stewardship and said he was pleased to contribute after learning about the rare lichen and NCC’s plans to study and protect it. The donation also marks a decade of conservancy’s work in the Salmonier area.What makes the boreal felt lichen habitat on Danny Williams' land so unusualBoreal felt lichens are particularly dependent on mature and over-mature balsam fir trees, as well as decaying trees, and thrive in cool, moist conditions. NCC says the species is especially sensitive to the loss of mature forest because clearing can create drier conditions and remove potential host trees. The Salmonier River area provides those conditions through its forests, wetlands and distinctive climate. The reserve lies in the Avalon Forest Ecoregion, Newfoundland’s smallest ecoregion, where frequent fog collects over low-lying, sheltered bogs. The protected landscape therefore preserves more than the rare lichens themselves.Which other at-risk species could benefit from the expanded Newfoundland nature reserveThe newly protected section of the Salmonier River Nature Reserve consists of forest and wetlands that provide habitat for several other species at risk. The conservancy identifies the red crossbill as threatened, while the olive-sided flycatcher is listed as special concern. The area also provides habitat for the little brown myotis and northern long-eared bat, both listed as endangered under Schedule 1 of the Species at Risk Act. The reserve also acts as a forested buffer for the 107,000-hectare Avalon Wilderness Reserve, which was established to protect barrens and forests supporting the Avalon woodland caribou herd, the most southerly caribou herd in Canada.You use AI every day. articles.title: PM Modi's convoy helicopter developed technical snag, remains stranded in Mysuru
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An Indian Air Force (IAF) helicopter, which was part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's convoy during his visit to Mysuru, developed a technical
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An Indian Air Force (IAF) helicopter, which was part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's convoy during his visit to Mysuru, developed a technical snag and remained grounded at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar helipad near Lalit Mahal on Friday.Three helicopters had arrived in Mysuru as part of the Prime Minister's convoy. However, one of the helicopters reportedly developed a technical problem while the convoy was preparing to leave after PM Modi's programme and could not take off.The Prime Minister and other members of the convoy subsequently continued their onward journey in one of the remaining two helicopters, while the aircraft that developed the snag remained parked at the helipad, according to news agency IANS.Meanwhile, local police have cordoned off the area around the helipad and stepped up security to protect the grounded aircraft. Staff members of the Mysuru City Corporation have also been deployed at the site as part of the arrangements.There was no official statement on the exact nature of the technical snag or when the aircraft would resume operations.Inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru PlanetariumPrime Minister Modi inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium as part of his Karnataka visit on Friday.Earlier, he participated in the golden jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA).He also flagged off and undertook a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station before inaugurating and laying the foundation stone for various development projects in Bengaluru.Following his engagements in Karnataka, PM Modi travelled to Gujarat, where he offered prayers and performed puja at the Ambaji Temple in Banaskantha district, one of the 51 revered Shakti Peethas.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Dragged by hair, beaten with sticks and fists:  Woman killed over Rs 500 owed by dead man; 6 arrested
articles.summary: RANCHI: Six people have been arrested for allegedly beating a 41-year-old woman to death following a dispute over Rs 500 in Jharkhand's West Singhbhum
articles.body: RANCHI: Six people have been arrested for allegedly beating a 41-year-old woman to death following a dispute over Rs 500 in Jharkhand's West Singhbhum district, police said on Saturday.The incident occurred around midnight on November 11 in Hadimara village, under the jurisdiction of Sonua police station.The accused were sitting around a fire outside the house of Reena Gope (32), whose husband had recently died, sub-divisional police officer (Chakradharpur) Syed Mustafa Hashmi said in a statement.The accused were warming themselves after performing the 'Markhi' (post-death ritual) of Reena's husband, Pandu Gope, when the victim, Jinggi Bankira, arrived and allegedly abused them, the officer said.Bankira was angry because Reena's late husband owed her Rs 500 and had died without repaying the amount, the SDPO said.Bankira fled and took shelter in an orchard behind her house. However, the accused chased her, found her and dragged her by her hair to the road, where they allegedly attacked her with sticks and fists.One of the accused, Krishna Gope, allegedly hit her on the head six to seven times with a stick, even after she had fallen to the ground. Bankira died of her injuries, the officer said.A case was registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) following a complaint lodged by the victim's son, Prem Singh Bankira, the next day.A special police team was constituted to investigate the case and apprehend the accused, Hashmi said.Based on evidence gathered during the investigation, police arrested Suraj Gope (25), Raghu Gope (19), Gukul Gope alias Langru (26), Reena Gope (32), Madhu Gope alias Koche, all residents of Hadimara village, and Krishna Gope, a resident of the Manoharpur police station area, on Thursday, he said.Police also recovered blood-stained sticks allegedly used in the crime, soil bearing bloodstains from the spot, a piece of a bangle and a pair of blood-stained jeans belonging to Raghu Gope, the officer added.(With inputs from PTI)Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Iran's navy says oil tanker on fire after hitting naval mine in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran's Navy said an oil tanker caught fire on Saturday morning after striking a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported.
articles.body: Iran's Navy said an oil tanker caught fire on Saturday morning after striking a naval mine in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. The vessel was reportedly disabled after entering a restricted maritime zone despite earlier warnings from Iranian authorities.Earlier the Navy also warned oil tankers against entering a restricted maritime zone east of the Strait of Hormuz after the vessel caught fire.According to Iran's state news agency ISNA, the Navy said the tanker had switched off its tracking and identification systems while sailing through what it described as an unsafe and restricted area, despite earlier warnings.The Navy cautioned that other tankers entering the prohibited zone could meet a similar fate. It also accused vessel owners of putting their assets at risk by relying on assurances from US President Donald Trump."It is regrettable that tanker owners, without learning from the fate of other rogue vessels, trusting the nonsense of the criminal US president, are sending their capital to the mine war and throwing it into the fire," the Navy's public relations department said, as reported by ISNA.The warning came hours after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claimed that two oil tankers attempting to cross the southern Strait of Hormuz without authorisation had exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines.The IRGC Navy also urged shipping companies not to cross the strategic waterway without coordinating with its Traffic Control Centre and following arrangements laid down by Iranian authorities.The incidents come amid escalating tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel, with the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a major flashpoint in the conflict.Iran has restricted maritime movement through the waterway following the US-Israeli military campaign against the country, which began on February 28. Tehran has maintained that vessels must obtain authorisation from Iranian authorities to ensure safe passage.The Strait of Hormuz is a strategically important international shipping route through which a significant share of the world's oil supply is transported.You use AI every day. articles.title: Deterring Russia becomes NATO's main effort as US scales back in Europe
articles.summary: NATO is weighing its biggest overhaul of military planning in at least two decades, and the question at its centre is simple: should the alliance prepare
articles.body: NATO is weighing its biggest overhaul of military planning in at least two decades, and the question at its centre is simple: should the alliance prepare to fight Russia in Europe, or to fight Russia in Europe and also run crises elsewhere? According to a Politico report, the 32 members have begun negotiations on new military capability requirements, which set the troops, weapons and funding countries must make available in a conflict.Under a draft planning document, members may no longer have to keep enough forces to fight a major war in Europe and, at the same time, carry out smaller crisis-management operations outside NATO territory. They could instead be asked to prepare for one scenario or the other. That would end a planning requirement in place for at least 20 years. It reflects the alliance's renewed focus on territorial defence since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and pressure from Washington to make European security NATO's main mission.Camille Grand, a former NATO assistant secretary-general for defence investment, said the proposal recognises that a major conflict in Europe would take priority over everything else. Oana Lungescu, a former NATO spokesperson, backed the shift, arguing that deterring Russia should be the alliance's main effort, particularly as the US reduces its military commitment to Europe. The change would not automatically affect missions in Kosovo and Iraq, and officials stress that NATO is not abandoning crisis response. Talks are at an early stage, with the Political Guidance document due by February and new capability requirements by 2029.Why the urgencyThe reasoning rests on warnings from think tanks. The Royal United Services Institute in London says there is now a credible threat of peer-level conflict in Europe by 2030, and that the question is no longer whether a war is possible but whether Europe is prepared to fight one.The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) in Washington goes further. In a report published on September 16, 2026, it said Russia is stepping up a coordinated campaign against European countries, including sabotage of critical infrastructure, attacks on defence industry facilities, cyber operations, assassination plots, airspace violations and threats to undersea cables. ISW argues these are coordinated, state-directed attacks and not isolated incidents or merely hybrid warfare.It also warned that Moscow could attempt a limited incursion, possibly against a Baltic state, to test NATO's unity and its willingness to invoke Article 5, the collective defence clause. Such a move could come before the 2028 to 2030 window cited by several members, with some assessments suggesting Russia could restore combat readiness by 2027.ISW urged European countries to speed up preparedness, protect critical infrastructure and learn from Ukraine. NATO, it said, must combine conventional capabilities such as armour, artillery and air power with drones and electronic warfare, and not depend on either traditional or drone-centric strategies alone.If the proposal goes through, it will show how quickly a conflict on Europe's eastern edge has changed what the world's biggest military alliance plans to be ready for.

articles.title: Bangladesh completes legal process for Hasina's return, leaves decision to India: Report
articles.summary: Bangladesh has completed the legal formalities required to seek the return of ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India, with its law minister
articles.body: Bangladesh has completed the legal formalities required to seek the return of ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India, with its law minister Asaduzzaman saying that the next step rests with New Delhi."We have completed everything required from our side as part of the legal process. What they (India) will do is up to them," the minister told reporters on Saturday, according to a report by Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo.The remarks came amid renewed speculation over Hasina's possible return to Bangladesh, after she reportedly expressed her intention to go back in December. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India under the two countries' extradition treaty.Asked whether Hasina would be given a legal opportunity to return, Asaduzzaman said she would come back through legal means, adding that extradition under the treaty would itself constitute a legal process."Sheikh Hasina will return to Bangladesh through legal means. We have completed everything required from our side as part of the legal process," he said.The minister was speaking to journalists after an event at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka.Hasina, who was ousted following the July 2024 mass uprising, was sentenced to death in a crimes against humanity case linked to the killings during the protests.The Bangladesh government has been asking India to hand her over under the prisoner transfer treaty. New Delhi has not yet responded to the extradition request.Referring to Article 47(3) of the 1973 law, Asaduzzaman said a person accused or convicted of crimes against humanity cannot claim fundamental rights.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'How were 2024 elections legitimate?' Rahul accuses EC of declaring 140 million who voted illegal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections while addressing the Bharat Summit in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections while addressing the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. He accused the Election Commission of declaring 140 million people who voted in the polls either "non-existent voters or non-voters"."If the Election Commission declares 140 million voters illegal, how is the election possibly legitimate?" the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha said."140 million people who voted in the 2024 Lok Sabha election were declared as either non-existent voters or non-voters a few months ago... If the election commission has declared 140 million voters, who supposedly voted in the 2024 elections, approximately 13% of Indian voters, illegal non-voters, then how is that election possibly legitimate?" he said.Rahul Gandhi also traced what he described as the erosion of Indian democracy to the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, alleging that the polls marked an unprecedented shift in the country's electoral system."In 2014, we witnessed a completely new election, something we had never seen before. Millions and millions and millions of dollars were injected into the political system," he said.He said the shift had overturned an electoral system that was earlier characterised by close contests and coalition governments. Rahul Gandhi added that the opposition was initially taken by surprise and took nearly a decade to understand the changes.Turning his attack towards the alleged nexus between big business and political power, Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of favouring businessman Gautam Adani, claiming that the distinction between the two had disappeared.Also read: Rahul Gandhi, Revanth Reddy ride pillion with gig workers during bike rally in Hyderabad - videoReferring to Adani's rise in the global wealth rankings, Gandhi said the businessman was ranked around 600th in the world before the BJP came to power but later became the world's second-richest person."How did he become the richest man? By a fusion between politics and business. The line between business and politics, between Adani and PM Modi, has evaporated. It does not exist anymore," he said, according to ANI.Rahul Gandhi further alleged that the BJP's assets had grown elevenfold in a decade, linking the party's financial growth to the concentration of political and economic power.Congress leader also accused the BJP of weakening democratic institutions and said the Congress had struggled to counter the ruling party because its traditional methods of political communication had stopped working.He also expressed confidence that the opposition would defeat Prime Minister Modi, claiming that the pressure on the BJP leadership was becoming increasingly visible. He said the Congress was determined to remove PM Modi from power and described the outcome as a certainty.At the summit, Rahul Gandhi also apologised to foreign delegates who could not attend the event in Hyderabad.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan's climate minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend SCO civilisational dialogue in New Delhi
articles.summary: Pakistan has nominated its federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, Musadik Masood Malik, to represent the country at the
articles.body: Pakistan has nominated its federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, Musadik Masood Malik, to represent the country at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) civilisational dialogue forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22."Pakistan to Participate in SCO Civilizational Dialogue in New Delhi The Government of Pakistan has nominated Dr Musadik Masood Malik, federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, to represent Pakistan at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue to be held in New Delhi from 20 to 22 November 2026," a government press release said."The event will bring together representatives from SCO member states to exchange views on issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding. The government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect," it added.The nomination comes a day after India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that invitations had been extended to several countries, including all 10 SCO member states, for the event.The inaugural forum is an Indian initiative aimed at promoting cultural exchange and people-to-people ties across the Eurasian region. India has also invited the grouping's observer states and dialogue partners.The SCO has 10 members: Belarus, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. articles.title: ‘Time to lower juvenile age to 16’: Kerala HC flags changing maturity levels
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Kerala High Court has suggested that the legal age threshold for juveniles be reduced from 18 to 16, saying children today show sufficient
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Kerala High Court has suggested that the legal age threshold for juveniles be reduced from 18 to 16, saying children today show sufficient maturity by the age of 16.The observation was made by Justice A Bhadarudeen during a hearing on a petition seeking stricter enforcement of laws prohibiting the sale and serving of liquor to people below 23 years of age, news agency PTI reported.Filed by Kollam resident Vinod Vikram, the petition cited the recent Nedumbassery accident in which an 18-year-old, allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol, rammed his Mini Cooper into a scooter, killing three people."That apart, it is high time for the legislatures to consider appropriate amendments in the statutes which deal with the 'juveniles and child in conflict' with law to reduce age to 16 years, taking note of the present trend showing sufficient maturity by children when they reach the age of 16. This aspect is also to be appropriately addressed," the court said in its interim order.Excise commissioner asked to submit reportThe court directed the Excise Commissioner to submit details of the steps taken to implement provisions of the Kerala Abkari Act. It also sought suggestions on how enforcement could be strengthened to protect the public.The matter will be heard again on November 24.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A New York apartment fire killed a woman whose family said their sixth-floor smoke alarm never worked and a fire door failed to close; a November 12 appeals court ruled their negligence lawsuit can proceed
articles.summary: A fire safety system is only as good as the equipment and people who maintain it.
articles.body: A fire safety system is only as good as the equipment and people who maintain it. A wrongful-death suit in a Manhattan apartment building raises questions about a faulty smoke alarm, a fire door that supposedly didn’t close and how a building superintendent responded to an emergency. Key negligence claims brought by the family of a deceased woman were allowed to move forward by the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department, on November 12, 2026, on the basis of significant factual disputes that justified additional review.Smoke alarm breakdowns at the heart of the disputeDe Los Santos v. 512-514 Realty LLC, is a lawsuit about a fatal fire at an apartment building at 512 West 136th Street in Manhattan. The plaintiffs alleged that the property owner failed to properly maintain the smoke alarms in the building, maintain the self-closing hinges on the door of apartment 4, where the fire apparently began, and provide adequate fire safety training to the building superintendent, said the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division.The family said the smoke alarm in their sixth-floor apartment never worked. Their deposition testimony also showed they heard no alarms or other audible warning devices during the fire.The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, held that conflicting testimony by the property owner's superintendent and vise president that the building had working alarms that sounded during and after the incident raised issues of fact. The court also said the owner did not prove that the alarms actually warned the dead woman and allowed her to escape safely.Further questions on fire door maintenanceAnother important issue in the appeal was the state of the door to apartment 4. Defending itself, the owner of the property cited a report done by an expert, who said that the door did not close because there was something in its way and not because of any faults in the hinges.But the plaintiffs offered evidence that the door had failed to close automatically when tenants had used it in the past. They also submitted photographs taken after the fire showing the open door with nothing in the doorway.The Appellate Division of the New York Supreme Court determined that the conflicting evidence raised a factual issue about whether the fire spread throughout the building because of poor maintenance of the door’s self-closing mechanism.Superintendent’s response subject to judicial reviewThe claims of negligence also became relevant to the actions of the superintendent once the fire started. Evidence presented to the court showed he opened the front entrance of the building and opened the basement doors. His testimony said that by keeping the front entrance open, smoke rose into the stairwell where the deceased woman was later discovered.The property owner has not resolved factual questions about whether the woman's death was caused by the lack of fire safety training, the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, said. The owner also failed to show that the fire went through the building by another action.Court of Appeals narrows, but upholds lawsuitThe appeals decision reversed an order issued by the New York County Supreme Court on March 5, 2026. The New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, affirmed the denial of summary judgment on the negligence claim but dismissed the separate claim for negligent infliction of emotional distress.The court said the plaintiffs did not present sufficient evidence to support that claim, noting testimony that a family member last saw the woman alive while the two were together in their sixth-floor apartment and did not see her injured.The ruling on November 12 leaves intact the family's main claims of negligence, but removes the emotional distress claim from the case. The ruling doesn’t assign fault to the property owner, but lets the unanswered questions about fire alarms, door maintenance and safety training proceed.Images Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: A Maryland county used AI cameras on school buses to generate 375,000 tickets and $92 million in fines; investigation finds little change in the violations they were meant to reduce
articles.summary: Montgomery County’s school bus cameras are facing questions over safety.
articles.body: Montgomery County’s school bus cameras are facing questions over safety. The Maryland county issued more than 375,000 tickets and $92 million in fines through its camera enforcement programme, but an investigation by Bloomberg Businessweek and Type Investigations found little reduction in violations and no evidence of fewer collisions near stopped school buses.​The findings raise questions about whether the programme is changing driver behaviour. BusPatrol, which operates the cameras, says its technology helps protect children while allowing local authorities to fund installation and operations through violation revenue. Its artificial intelligence cameras flag suspected illegal passing, but police review the evidence before issuing tickets. The $92 million represents fines issued, rather than money collected.​What the investigation found about violations​County figures cited in the investigation show that citations per active camera fell only slightly, from 36 in 2020 to 34 in 2025. Total citations increased over that period, from 50,698 to 51,779.​The investigation examined county records, local news reports and camera footage. Its finding of no evidence of fewer collisions does not establish that cameras have no safety value, but it questions whether the volume of tickets demonstrates the promised improvement.​How the camera programme is funded​Between fiscal years 2019 and 2024, Montgomery County retained about $18.5 million from collected fines while setting aside roughly $40 million for BusPatrol, according to the investigation.​BusPatrol says its financial arrangements allow it to recover installation and operating costs. The company also says it covers the shortfall when camera expenses exceed violation revenue.​The model allows school districts to install equipment without paying the full cost upfront. However, the investigation found that technology fees and revenue-sharing arrangements can leave participating authorities with a limited share of the proceeds.​How AI cameras identify suspected violations​The cameras record vehicles suspected of illegally passing stopped school buses. BusPatrol packages the evidence for police review, with officers deciding whether a citation should follow.​The distinction matters because an AI-generated flag is not a finding that a driver broke the law. Human review is still part of the enforcement process.​At the time of the investigation, BusPatrol had equipped about 35,000 buses in 24 states and more than 350 school districts. The company said its systems promote student safety and driver accountability and that official crash statistics don't account for near misses.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: SAD, BJP seat-sharing talks under way; formal announcement expected this month: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are holding discussions on seat-sharing for the 2027 Punjab assembly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are holding discussions on seat-sharing for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, with a formal announcement on a possible alliance expected later this month, news agency PTI reported on Saturday, citing sources from both parties.The talks come amid growing speculation that the former allies could reunite after ending their decades-old partnership in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.Union Jal Shakti minister and BJP's Punjab election in-charge C R Patil is expected to visit the state on November 17 and meet party leaders in Chandigarh, PTI reported citing sources. His visit comes as discussions around a possible alliance gain momentum.The speculation has also intensified following recent political engagements. Former Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi a few days ago and is learnt to have discussed issues concerning the state, including drug abuse.The two parties had shared power and contested elections together for several years before the SAD walked out of the alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws. Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement for Punjab Assembly elections, the SAD contested 94 seats and the BJP 23 of the state's 117 constituencies. In Lok Sabha polls, the SAD contested 10 seats and the BJP three.The BJP has since indicated that it is no longer willing to play a junior partner in Punjab and has maintained that it is preparing to contest all 117 assembly seats.In the 2022 Punjab assembly elections, the BJP won two seats, while the SAD secured three. The next assembly polls are due in 2027.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A former Amazon warehouse in Michigan now holds 125 of Ford's historic cars, from rare Le Mans racers to Hollywood Mustangs; the 79,000-square-foot Vault will welcome its first visitors on November 14
articles.summary: A former Amazon warehouse in Romulus, Michigan, has been turned into a home for 125 historically significant vehicles from Ford's collection.
articles.body: A former Amazon warehouse in Romulus, Michigan, has been turned into a home for 125 historically significant vehicles from Ford's collection. Called the Ford Vault, the 79,000-square-foot facility brings together more than a century of automotive history, including rare racing cars, concept vehicles, classic Mustangs and automobiles associated with television and popular culture.Ford is opens the doors of the new facility to select members of the public and company employees on Saturday. The special event was sold out, but the company says it plans to organise more opportunities for visitors to see the collection. According to ABC news, the vehicles were previously kept at Ford's headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan, and at other locations.The new facility is located inside a former Amazon fulfilment centre in Romulus, a suburb of Detroit. It provides a single space for Ford's Heritage Fleet, which includes vehicles that played important roles in the company's history. The collection features racing cars, design experiments, historic trucks and vehicles that became part of American popular culture.Ford says the facility is not just meant to preserve old vehicles. It has also been designed as a working archive where the company's designers, engineers and other employees can study earlier models and ideas. The aim is to give them access to the designs and experiments that shaped Ford as they work on future vehicles.Ted Ryan, Ford's archives and heritage brand manager, said the company did not want to keep the collection hidden from the public.“You don’t create an experience like this and a space like this and then hide it away,” Ryan said. “We’re going to find a way to make it available to the car community in Michigan as soon as we can.”Ford Vault brings together 125 historic vehiclesThe collection includes 125 vehicles from Ford's Heritage Fleet. These range from cars built for motorsport to concept models that helped shape later production vehicles. It also includes automobiles connected with films, television shows and other aspects of popular culture.Ciera Casteel, Ford's archives manager, said the new facility gives the vehicles a dedicated space. “Here, we can actually have a purpose-built space for the cars,” she said as quoted by ABC news. “That's our legacy. That's what we do here. That is what this company is.”Among the vehicles on display are the first three cars to cross the finish line at the 1966 24 Hours of Le Mans. The race became widely known through the 2019 film Ford v Ferrari, starring Matt Damon and Christian Bale. The three cars are among the collection's major highlights and represent an important part of Ford's racing history.Another unusual exhibit is a 2005 Mustang GT proof-of-concept. The vehicle helped pave the way for the Shelby GT350. Engineers gave it the nickname “Johnny Cash”, inspired by the singer's song “One Piece at a Time”. The song tells the story of an autoworker who builds a car using mismatched parts.The prototype has undergone several changes over the years, with different components added to it. Ryan compared its appearance to Frankenstein because of the parts attached to it.“It's like Frankenstein. Things have been bolted onto Johnny over the years. This is the first time he's ever been displayed,” he said.From a British-built Model T to a television MustangThe Vault also contains vehicles that have unusual histories beyond their connection with Ford. One of them is a 1910 right-hand-drive Model T built in the United Kingdom. The car remained there until 2025, when it became part of Ford's Heritage Fleet. Its inclusion adds an example of the company's early international vehicle production to the collection.Another notable vehicle is a 1973 Mustang convertible featured in The Mary Tyler Moore Show. The car was sold in 1974 and remained in private ownership for several decades. Ford bought it last year and brought it into the historic collection.The Mustang's body underwent restoration work in 1999, but its interior remains original. Its connection with the television show makes it one of the vehicles that demonstrate Ford's presence in popular culture.The collection also includes Jay Leno's 1934 Flathead Ford pickup truck, along with historic police cruisers, a 1938 ambulance and several concept vehicles.These vehicles show the different types of automobiles Ford has produced or developed over the years. The collection brings together models associated with racing, everyday transport, vehicle design and entertainment.A working archive for Ford's designers and engineersThe Ford Vault has been developed as more than an exhibition space. The company wants its employees to use the collection to understand earlier designs and learn from the ideas behind them.Designers and engineers will be able to examine older vehicles closely and study how their features changed over time. The collection is expected to provide references for employees working on new designs.One example highlighted by Ford is the first F-150 built at the Rouge complex. Its design looks considerably different from the trucks currently being produced there, showing how the vehicle has changed over the years.Gordon Platto, Ford's design director, said seeing the vehicles in person could spark ideas and influence the design process.The company took about three years to develop the facility. articles.title: Putin's grandson registered with mother's surname as father's name resembles Ukraine President Zelenskyy’s: Report
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin's grandson Adrian was registered under his mother's surname, Tikhonov, after being born to Katerina Tikhonova and ballet dancer Igor Zelensky. The unusual name choice raises eyebrows amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin's grandson was registered under his mother's surname rather than his father's, according to a report by the news outlet Agentsvo. The child, Adrian, is the son of Putin's daughter Katerina Tikhonova and ballet dancer Igor Zelensky.Adrian was born on August 15, 2025, but his birth was registered only 11 months later, the report said. His surname was recorded as Tikhonov, the masculine form of his mother's family name.The choice has drawn attention because his father shares the surname Zelensky with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, although the two men are not related. Putin has been leading Russia's war against Ukraine since February 2022.The reason behind the delayed registration and the decision to use Tikhonov instead of Zelensky remains unclear. According to the report, delay could be linked to efforts by the president's family to keep the birth private or complications arising from the parents having different surnames.Who are Adrian's parents, Katerina Tikhonova and Igor Zelensky?Tikhonova, 40, is Putin's daughter from his marriage to former wife Lyudmila Ocheretnaya. She is a former rock-and-roll dancer who has since become a technology executive involved in major Russian artificial intelligence projects.Her partner, Igor Zelensky, 57, is a ballet dancer and artistic director who previously led the Bavarian State Ballet in Germany. He has no family connection to Ukraine's president.The couple also have an older daughter, Elsa, who is now eight. At birth, she was registered using the feminine form of her father's surname, Zelenskaya. She is now believed to use Tikhonova, according to the report.Russian law requires births to be registered within the month following a child's arrival. Adrian's registration, which took place 11 months after his birth, therefore came considerably later than the usual deadline.What is known about Putin's other children and grandchildren?Putin's family details have largely remained outside public view. According to the report, all five of his children use names different from his surname.Tikhonova has an older sister, Maria Vorontsova, 41, who was also born during Putin's marriage to Ocheretnaya. Vorontsova has two children, including a grandson who is half-Dutch.Putin is also reported to have two sons with his partner, Alina Kabaeva, 43. Ivan, 11, and Vladimir, eight, reportedly use the surname Spiridonov rather than Putin.The surname is believed to have been taken from Putin's paternal grandfather, Spiridon Putin, who lived from 1879 to 1965. Spiridon worked as a personal chef to Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin and later prepared meals for Lenin's widow, Nadezhda, and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin. He had also served Grigori Rasputin while working at the Hotel Astoria in St Petersburg.Putin is further reported to have a daughter, Luiza Rozova, 23, from his relationship with Svetlana Krivinogikh, 51. Krivinogikh, who previously worked as a cleaner, later became a wealthy businesswoman with interests in banking and the nightclub industry.Rozova has reportedly spent time living in Paris rather than Russia.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trumpiana: To hell with heaven!
articles.summary: For the sweet taste of revenge, Donald may even skip paradise Make way Abe Lincoln.
articles.body: For the sweet taste of revenge, Donald may even skip paradiseMake way Abe Lincoln. ‘Honest Donald’ is here and he is in no mood to forgive his enemies even if it costs him a place in heaven where he ardently hopes to go after death.“The answer is no. I want to be honest, no,” Trump told ‘60 Minutes,’ when asked if he could forgive some of his enemies before the judgment throne of God, “Because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will.”How could he forgive those “very bad people” who had given him hell, said the President, who had last year too rated his chances of getting in low. “I’m hearing I’m not doing well. I am really at the bottom of the totem pole,” he then told his favourite ‘Fox & Friends’ without revealing his sources up there.But even as he aired his honest belief that the Republicans got a midterm drubbing because he was not on the ballot although he had asked voters to pretend he was, Trump acknowledged his deportation campaign may have been “too tough.”He also blamed “bad messaging” for voters’ affordability concerns in the interview two days after he replaced chief of staff Ice Maiden Susie Wiles with fiery immigration hawk Stephen Miller, signalling not less, but more Trumpism that led to his — oops his party’s debacle.Then days after saying he was “absolutely willing” to accept the midterm results, Trump returned to his usual refrain that Democrats stole the midterms suggesting their victories weren’t “honest.”“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest? How could the Polls be so wrong???” he posted on Truth Social ignoring the fact that the polls had only underestimated the size of the Democratic sweep.‘Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote,” suggested Trump again blaming without any basis “unreliable” voting machines.And as newly elected Democrats made clear their intentions to launch congressional probes when they gain control in January, the White House geared up to fight back with a battery of new lawyers and a warning missive about “monitoring” Democrats’ “abusive and capricious threats.”Then just a couple of days after suggesting there is no need for new strikes against Iran with peace negotiations making progress, Trump ordered Vice President JD Vance to pull out of the talks and focus on corruption at home — of the Democratic variety.In a Truth Social post, Trump said he was redirecting Vance to focus his “complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.”“We don’t need a deal with Iran,” he wrote. “Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”A day earlier, in a Veterans Day address at Arlington National Cemetery, Trump had declared U.S. will accept nothing less than “total victory” over Iran though it has already won the war and that it is “just a question of when we want to end it.”Amid reports of Democratic lawmakers expanding their quid pro quo probe of the donors of his big beautiful ballroom and nine Kennedy family members joining a lawsuit against his triumphal arch, Trump suggested it would also be dedicated to the U.S. military and its ranks.Some military groups have cheered the 250-foot arch inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, that Trump himself has suggested might even be called the “Arc de Trump.’’But many others have opposed it with the Kennedy family fearing it would “permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sightlines” in the nearby cemetery, including the eternal flame at the assassinated 35th President John F. Kennedy’s grave site.Meanwhile, a guerrilla art group the Secret Handshake installed a new statue on the National Mall mocking Trump for allegedly dodging the Vietnam war draft in 1968 with a bone spurs diagnosis.Titled The Foot Soldier, the gilded statue depicts Trump sitting down while rubbing his bare foot. “We salute a leader who knows you can’t spell sacrifice without ‘I,’ and a warrior who reminds us that sometimes when you’re called to stand up, it’s best to just sit down and rest your feet,” reads the plaque.“Draft dodger? I hardly know her,” a person dressed as “Toey”, a 6ft-tall mascot of a toe suffering from bone spurs, told the Washington Post, “I’m the biggest toe. The hugest toe. Huge. Hugest toe. Largest toe that anyone’s ever seen.”A White House spokesperson was quick to dismiss the art work as yet another manifestation of “Trump Derangement Syndrome” calling it “a sick and incurable disease that has rotted the brains of these Democrat activists.”Earlier, in one of his own pranks, Trump set the cat among scribes by offering the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the CEO and president of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).The announcement was accompanied by an animated AI cartoon showing UFC fighters throwing out journalists asking inconvenient questions. At the end, as Trump peeps in to ask, “How was the briefing?” White gleefully responds, “fiery but mostly peaceful.”Trump later assured horrified reporters he “was only kidding” to bring home the point that with UFC boss flanked by six fighters around, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much.”No kidding, maybe Trump was only offering a preview of his plan B to crash the pearly gates with sheer muscle power!(The article is an arrangement with The American Bazaar)You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump, Xi, Putin meet next week: Why the 1945 Yalta Conference is back in focus
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to meet in China's Shenzhen next week on the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to meet in China's Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, raising concerns that the three major powers could discuss global issues and reach understandings without involving countries directly affected by them.Negotiations over the proposed meeting are still under way, with no agenda or format finalised, according to two people familiar with the discussions cited by news agency Reuters. Topics under consideration include the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence.Why comparisons with Yalta ConferenceThe proposed gathering has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, held in Crimea towards the end of World War II. US President Franklin D Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met there to discuss the post-war settlement, including the division of influence in Europe.The conference helped shape the political order that emerged after the war and became associated with major powers deciding the fate of smaller countries.The comparison has resurfaced because Ukraine and other countries fear that a Trump-Putin-Xi meeting could lead to decisions on territorial disputes, security arrangements or spheres of influence without their participation."We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4,' with a redistribution of influence," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last month.Three leaders, different prioritiesThe three leaders are approaching the proposed talks with different priorities. Putin is seeking discussions on ending the Ukraine war, while Trump has expressed interest in nuclear arms control. China, which has a considerably smaller nuclear arsenal than the US and Russia, has been reluctant to engage in such discussions.A senior Trump administration official said, "we do not expect to get to any kind of agreement" on nuclear issues, but added that "it's time for China to sort of step up".China's embassy in Washington said it was in communication with relevant parties but had nothing to share.Putin's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said: "Suggestions are being exchanged regarding a possible agenda." He added that the meeting would "certainly be interesting" and attract global attention.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A fake GoFundMe appeared less than 24 hours after a pregnant mother of four died in an Amtrak crash; her family said scammers used her photographs to collect donations
articles.summary: A fake GoFundMe campaign was created less than 24 hours after a pregnant mother of four died in an Amtrak crash in Jacksonville, Florida, prompting her
articles.body: A fake GoFundMe campaign was created less than 24 hours after a pregnant mother of four died in an Amtrak crash in Jacksonville, Florida, prompting her family to warn the public about online donation scams. Lakeisha Jennings, who was around four months pregnant, died when an Amtrak train struck her Jeep. According to her relatives, the fraudulent fundraiser used photographs of Jennings and her family to collect donations. While the family appealed to GoFundMe to remove the fake page, they also confirmed a separate legitimate campaign established by Arcadia Brown to help cover funeral expenses. The incident has raised concerns about scammers targeting grieving families.Jennings' family asks GoFundMe to remove fake fundraiser using her photosJennings' relatives have asked GoFundMe to remove the fraudulent campaign, which they said had used personal photographs of the deceased woman and her family. Oliver explained that the situation had made an already difficult period more distressing, particularly as the family was trying to organise Jennings' funeral.Oliver also expressed concern about the circumstances surrounding the fundraiser, saying that the family was working to give Jennings' daughter an unforgettable farewell. She described the alleged scam as selfish and said it had added to the emotional burden on relatives who were already coping with their loss.Family shares legitimate GoFundMe page after fraudulent fundraiser emergesAmid concerns about the fraudulent page, Jennings' family confirmed that a separate, legitimate GoFundMe campaign had been established for Arcadia Brown to help cover her funeral expenses. As News4JAX reported, the family had verified this fundraiser and linked the authentic campaign to its report so that people wishing to contribute could identify the correct page.The family also warned that scammers could target other people experiencing bereavement or seeking financial assistance. Oliver said she believed such incidents happened frequently, explaining that scammers could use publicly available information, including obituaries, to identify deceased individuals and approach grieving families.Cybersecurity expert warns how small donations can add up in online scamsGoFundMe by email and filed a complaint about the fraudulent fundraising page. According to the report, the fake campaign had already collected hundreds of dollars. GoFundMe's Giving Guarantee states that donors may be eligible for a refund within one year if a fundraiser is determined to be fraudulent.Cybersecurity expert Ian Marlow, chief executive of Fitech, explained that even relatively small contributions could accumulate into substantial amounts when fundraising pages circulated widely online. He cited donations of $20, $50 and $100 as examples of amounts that could add up, particularly if a campaign went viral. Marlow advised donors to exercise caution before contributing, recommending that they verify the legitimacy of a website and email and check with other people who may have donated. articles.title: From smarter bins to safer borders, young minds engineer change
articles.summary: Synergia’26 in Mangaluru saw students showcase AI/IoT projects: EcoBin AI waste sorting, Agrisense crop disease detection, Thameri safety lights, border rover tech.
articles.body: Mangaluru: What if a dustbin could sort your garbage in seconds, a photograph could help save a farmer’s crop, or a streetlight could guide a woman to safety without even needing a mobile network? For young innovators from Dakshina Kannada, these are no longer just ideas but working prototypes that put technology to work on everyday challenges.These innovations were among the highlights of Synergia’26, the three-day annual innovation festival hosted by Sahyadri College of Engineering and Management at Adyar, where high school and pre-university students showcased projects using artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) to address civic, agricultural, public safety and defence challenges.Taking on the city’s waste management problem, five Class 12 students from St Aloysius Pre-University College — Arol Sequeira, Ashfar Abdul Khader, Alwin Sijo, Thejaswi K and Prithvi D Suvarna — developed ‘EcoBin AI’, an automated waste segregator. Using computer vision, load sensors and a four-quadrant rotary carousel, it classifies plastic, metal and paper in 1.2 seconds and isolates contaminated waste. Users can scan a QR code to earn redeemable points. “Automating segregation at the point of disposal prevents cross-contamination and keeps dry recyclables clean,” said team lead Arol.At Padua Pre-University College, students Shaina Lisha Monthero, Diganth U Poojary, Glanston D’Souza and Deekshitha R P presented ‘Agrisense’. The platform uses soil-moisture sensors and machine learning to identify crop diseases from leaf photographs with 97% accuracy. It also recommends crops based on soil and weather conditions and offers multilingual treatment advice.Women’s safety in poorly connected areas inspired ‘Thameri – Safety Beacon Network 2.0’, developed by four students of Sharada Shubhodaya Vidyalaya, Moodushedde. Its solar-powered streetlights work without mobile networks or Wi-Fi. Pressing an emergency button activates nearby sirens, alerts control rooms and illuminates safe routes. “The system guides people towards the nearest safe zone,” said team member Nihal C A.Meanwhile, Team Quantumbots of Carmel Pre-University College, Modankap, showcased ‘Border Suraksha Kawach’ and the ‘Mushak Rover’. The low-cost system detects human intrusion along unfenced borders and allows soldiers to deploy a remotely operated rover with a 360-degree live camera from a safety bunker.Shortlisted among the top 100 entries for the national-level Young Scientist of India event in Chennai on Nov 19, the team hopes to enter the top 20 with an upgraded system featuring thermal night-vision cameras and drone detection, team leader Krishna said.BOX1. articles.title: Four killed, three critical in two Chhattisgarh road accidents
articles.summary: Four people died and three were critically injured in two Chhattisgarh road accidents in Mahasamund and Bemetara; police are investigating both crashes.
articles.body: Raipur: Four people, including two women travelling in an ambulance, were killed and three others critically injured in two separate road accidents in Chhattisgarh’s Mahasamund and Bemetara districts between Friday night and Saturday morning.An ambulance transporting a patient to Odisha rammed into a stationary truck on NH-353, while two relatives riding a motorcycle died in a crash on the Bemetara-Durg road.In Mahasamund, the ambulance, carrying a patient and accompanying persons from a hospital towards Odisha, crashed into the rear of a truck parked near a school on the national highway in the Bagbahara area on Saturday morning.The impact mangled the front portion of the ambulance, killing two women on the spot and seriously injuring three others, including two women and a man.According to preliminary reports, the ambulance was returning towards Odisha after the patient received treatment in Mahasamund. The circumstances in which the driver failed to notice the stationary truck are under investigation.Local residents rushed to the spot after hearing the collision and alerted the police. Rescue personnel, assisted by villagers, pulled the injured occupants from the wreckage and shifted them to the Bagbahara community health centre.After emergency treatment, doctors referred the three injured persons to another hospital for advanced medical care in view of their critical condition.Police sent the bodies of the two women for postmortem examination and began efforts to establish the identities of the deceased and the injured. Preliminary information suggested that the occupants were from Odisha.Investigators are examining whether the truck was parked in a designated area, whether adequate warning signals were in place, and what caused the ambulance to crash into it.Reports also suggested that the ambulance driver left the scene after the collision, although police confirmation was awaited.In the other accident, two men were killed when their motorcycle met with an accident near Ninwa village on the Bemetara-Durg main road late on Friday night.The deceased were identified as Kedar Jaiswal (62) and his brother-in-law Govardhan Sinha (50).The duo was travelling from Bemetara towards Durg on the motorcycle when the accident occurred. articles.title: Who is Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins? Democrat wins Alaska governor's race for first time since 1998
articles.summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won Alaska's gubernatorial election, ending the Republican Party's hold on the state's governor's office for the
articles.body: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won Alaska's gubernatorial election, ending the Republican Party's hold on the state's governor's office for the first time since 1998. His victory comes as Democrats make significant gains across state governments in the 2026 US midterm elections.Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state lawmaker, defeated three Republican candidates, including one endorsed by US President Donald Trump. His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, after flipping several states that had been under Republican control for years, including Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.The 37-year-old, popularly known as JKT, is making a political comeback three years after leaving the Alaska state House. He built support by travelling across the state and focusing his campaign on affordability, public education and economic issues.Who is Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins?Kreiss-Tomkins is a former Alaska state representative who returned to electoral politics after leaving the state House three years ago.During his campaign, he called for full funding of public schools and proposed requiring all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income tax. He also advocated a moratorium on new data centres until state lawmakers establish regulations governing their development.He criticised outgoing Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy, who has been in office for eight years, saying Alaska had become "broken" and needed a change.Among the issues he highlighted was the state's ferry system, which he said had been left in poor condition, with services to several communities drastically reduced. Ferries are an important mode of transport for communities in southeast Alaska that are not connected by roads and have limited air connectivity.How did Kreiss-Tomkins defeat Trump's backed candidate?Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republican candidates: Bernadette Wilson, Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor.Trump had endorsed Wilson, a businesswoman, while criticising the other Republican candidates for remaining in the race.Kreiss-Tomkins had finished first in Alaska's August open primary. Another Democrat, Tom Begich, who came second, subsequently withdrew and backed him, saying consolidating Democratic voters, donors and resources behind one candidate offered the strongest chance of victory.Wilson had finished third in the primary.The Democrat also received support from Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski, who has occasionally differed with her party and Trump. She endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins a week before the election, saying he understood the importance of listening to people with different perspectives and finding common ground.Three former Alaska governors, Democrat Tony Knowles, independent Bill Walker and Republican Frank Murkowski, also endorsed him.What did Kreiss-Tomkins promise as Alaska governor?Kreiss-Tomkins campaigned on a promise to work across party lines and said he wanted his administration to include Republicans, Democrats and independents."If they're competent, if they're service-minded, if they're entrepreneurial, if they're problem-solvers, you're on the team. Game on," he said during a candidate forum last month.In a statement declaring victory, he said voters wanted change and a government that could work across party lines to address Alaska's problems. He added that his campaign had received contributions from more than 10,000 donors.He also described compromise as "a virtue, not a dirty word", saying his responsibility would be to work with lawmakers to resolve longstanding problems in the state.When will Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins take office?Kreiss-Tomkins is set to be sworn in as Alaska's governor on December 7. His running mate, independent Zac Johnson, will serve as lieutenant governor.Alaska's last Democratic governor was Tony Knowles, who left office in 2002 after serving two consecutive terms. Independent Bill Walker subsequently governed the state from 2014 to 2018.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Abhishek Banerjee questioned for 4 hours by Kolkata’s Bhowanipore police over an FIR linked to his X post on CEC Gyanesh Kumar; may be summoned again.
articles.body: Kolkata: Trinamool national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee was questioned by Bhowanipore police for nearly four hours on Saturday in connection with an FIR for his social media post against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Banerjee arrived at 12.23 pm, seven minutes ahead of his scheduled summons, and left around 4.30 pm. Police sources said his response was being studied and he might be called again if needed.BJP workers raised “chor” (thief) slogans while Banerjee was inside. As he emerged from the police station, TMC supporters countered by accusing BJP of paying demonstrators to shout slogans, and attacked state govt over high unemployment and delay in the Annapurna scheme’s rollout.Banerjee was summoned in a May 27 FIR filed by one Arnabkanti Das, who alleged that in his May 2 post on X, the MP described CEC Kumar as a “puppet of an anti-Bengali Gujarati gang”.Police booked Banerjee under BNS provisions relating to promoting enmity, inciting violence, spreading rumours, provoking offences against the state and causing public disorder.Speaking to reporters after the questioning, Banerjee said: “Whenever officials have summoned me, I have gone. I am being called in various false cases. I am appearing because of the high court’s directive. If they call me again, I will go. Based on one post, they questioned me as much as they wanted and I cooperated.”The TMC MP also claimed to have explained why he said “Gujarati gang”. “BJP believes Bengali is not even a language; they say there is only a Bangladeshi language. Amit Malviya had called Bengali a Bangladeshi language,” he added.Banerjee also launched a sharp attack on CM Suvendu Adhikari, asking why he had not faced similar summons in the Narada case.Addressing the recent demolition drive outside his residence, Banerjee said while he did not object to the removal of govt structures or police camps, authorities must not jeopardise the livelihoods of local artisans. “Please do not evict those who are working along the footpaths here. If you want to run a bulldozer, run it over my house. If you want revenge, take it on me, because you cannot fight me politically,” he said.State minister Dilip Ghosh, reacting to Banerjee’s appearance before the police, said: “He has been summoned multiple times by ED, CBI and others earlier as well. This saga will continue.”Trinamool had failed to shed its “feudal” mindset even after its electoral defeat, Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said, adding: “There is a saying ‘rassi jal gayi, par bal nahi gaya.”Banerjee has also been summoned by Girish Park police on Nov 20 in a separate FIR over derogatory remarks and threats against a serving officer in the state.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Man loses Rs 4.5 lakh in WFH scam
articles.summary: Mangaluru man loses Rs 4.5 lakh in work-from-home scam after being lured via WhatsApp and Telegram with fake tasks and investment returns; case filed.
articles.body: Mangaluru: A 28-year-old man who earns his livelihood through dairy farming and agriculture on his own land, was allegedly cheated of Rs 4.5 lakh by cyber fraudsters on the pretext of offering part-time work-from-home opportunities.According to the complaint, the victim was looking for a part-time job and had uploaded his resume on a website in Sept.On Nov 3, he was added to a WhatsApp group. Subsequently, a person identifying herself as Neha Sharma and claiming to be an employee of a private company, offered part-time work-from-home opportunities. She told him that he could earn between Rs 50 and Rs 200 daily by completing tasks assigned by the company. Believing the offer, the complainant agreed to take up the work and completed the assigned tasks. He was initially paid for completing them, which strengthened his confidence in the scheme.On Nov 4, he was introduced to a scheme under which he was promised a profit of Rs 1,200 for investments ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 18,000. He initially invested a small amount and received the promised returns. Convinced that the scheme was genuine, he allegedly transferred a total of Rs 4.5 lakh in multiple transactions between Nov 4 and 11, from his own and his mother’s bank accounts to various bank accounts and UPI IDs.The complainant alleged that unidentified persons had contacted him through WhatsApp and Telegram groups, lured him into investing increasing amounts. articles.title: ‘Bhool gaya’ moment! Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s hilarious response at toss on record-breaking captaincy debut - Watch
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his captaincy debut for Bihar at just 15 years old. After winning the toss, he humorously forgot his team's playing XI moments late...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had a memorable and amusing moment during his historic captaincy debut on Saturday when the 15-year-old forgot Bihar's playing XI after winning the toss against Saurashtra in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 opener at the Holkar Stadium. Asked about his team's combination after opting to bat, Sooryavanshi responded with a smile: "I think, sir, bhool gaya lagta main (I think, sir, I have forgotten)." The light-hearted exchange quickly became a talking point on a landmark day for the teenage batting sensation, who became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history at 15 years and 232 days. Sooryavanshi broke the previous record held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who had captained his national side at 17 years and 311 days in a T20 International against Cyprus on August 7, 2025.

'Dream come true': Sooryavanshi on leading Bihar

The Bihar youngster described the opportunity to captain his home state as a special moment, expressing gratitude for being entrusted with the responsibility. "It feels like a dream come true because I started playing cricket here, and getting the opportunity to lead the same state is a big thing. I am very grateful, and I will try to fulfil the responsibility given to me to the best of my ability," he said. WATCH:

Bihar handed Sooryavanshi the leadership role for their first two matches of the domestic T20 competition. The appointment marks another milestone in his rapid rise, having made his India debut just five months ago. He was also named vice-captain of East Zone for the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy, deputising for Ishan Kishan. His first outing as Bihar captain, however, did not produce a substantial contribution with the bat. Sooryavanshi scored 18 off 12 deliveries before being caught and bowled by left-arm pacer Chetan Sakariya. Bihar managed 137/9 in their 20 overs, with Prithvi Raj top-scoring with 38. Saurashtra chased down the target in 16.3 overs to register a five-wicket victory. Harvansh Pangalia led the chase with 33 off just 11 balls, hitting three sixes and three fours.

Short SMAT stint before India A assignment

Sooryavanshi is expected to feature in only one more SMAT match before joining India A for the ACC Rising Stars Emerging tournament in Doha from November 19. His latest international outing came during India's T20I tour of New Zealand, where he scored 49 runs in two matches. His 19-ball 45, featuring in a 133-run opening stand with Abhishek Sharma in just 7.1 overs, was among the highlights of India's 3-2 series victory.
